results.reason: Consistency is not defined through the optimal decoder: the paper says it is exactly the accuracy of the Gibbs decoder, and the optimal deterministic decoder only bounds it within a factor of two in error. What makes both unbounded is that each uses the exact conditional distribution Pr(y|pi) of the model's labels given the explanation. The conclusion holds, but the stated reason names the wrong decoder.
evidence: dasgupta2022framework [P40]: "(i) the (randomized) Gibbs decoder that, given explanation π, returns a label y with probability Pr(y|π), and (ii) the optimal deterministic decoder that returns the label y that maximizes Pr(y|π)"
dasgupta2022framework [P40]: "Our notion of consistency is exactly the accuracy of the Gibbs decoder: m c = 1 − EG ."
results.replacement: Both decoders in Dasgupta et al. use the exact distribution $\Pr(y\mid\pi)$ of the model's labels given the explanation, so consistency does not model a bounded human or monitor.
